name: Dependency network
reader_question: Which organisations, projects and programmes depend on which, and what is the path between two of them?
relationship: Directed acyclic network laid out in computed layers; edges are declared dependencies, one path is highlighted.
use_when: Declared links between named entities explain an exposure or a chain of supply or funding
avoid_when: Link sizes matter — use conversion-flow or sources-and-uses
The graph has cycles or hundreds of nodes — use a table of links

data_contract.notes: What an arrow means, shown in the legend
Up to 20 directed edges between adjacent computed layers; no duplicates, no cycles
Node ids; every consecutive pair must be a declared edge

units: No quantities; edges carry no weight.

editable: Node boxes, arrows and labels as native shapes and text
not_data_bound: Nodes and edges are drawn shapes at computed positions; arrows are not PowerPoint connectors and do not follow moved boxes

variations: Columns by entity type instead of computed layer
Edge labels where a source names each relationship
limitations: Edges must join adjacent layers; add the intermediate node otherwise
Layout is a deterministic heuristic and may not minimise crossings for dense graphs
A drawn link is a declared dependency, not evidence of its size or importance

excluded_alternatives.reason: Positions carry no meaning and change between builds
Implies quantified flow; the edges here are unweighted
